text.p: Finnish forest industry group Enso Oy on Monday reported halved profits in 1996 and forecast a rise in sales volumes to enable similar earnings this year despite a slow recovery in prices.
Enso's profit after financial items was 1.67 billion markka ($328 million), less than half the 3.52 billion profit posted in 1995. Net sales fell to 25.66 billion markka from 28.03 billion.

"The result for the year as a whole is expected to be about the same as in 1996," the company said. "Enso expects its sales volumes to be higher than last year, but prices will improve only slowly from their present low levels."

Though last year's profit was slightly above the 1.58 billion median of analysts forecasts, Enso's stock fell 1.50 markka to 44.00 in moderate trade after the announcement, paring strong gains last week.
Profits at the start of the year would be weaker than in the year-ago period, but the overall outlook for the most important business areas was improving, Enso said.
"Paper consumption is rising, and this will stimulate demand and raise capacity utilisation rates at the mills," it said.
"Despite the increase in orders for paper products, price rises are likely to be slow in coming, as chemical pulp stocks were still above normal at the start of the year," it said.
New capacity would boost supply particularly in coated fine papers this year, it said.
"The trend in costs is expected to be moderate," Enso said.
